Sakha

PhD Applicant — Software Engineering, Computer Science, LLMs, Generative & Agentic AI, Trustworthy and Safe AI Systems

MS in Software Engineering with hands-on experience in agent-based systems (agent creation and communication), LLMs, tokenization and transformers, CNN / 1D-CNN / LSTM-Attention models and code generation and clone analysis. I work through the full ML pipeline: data exploration and analysis, preprocessing, data modeling, training and model evaluation, using Python scientific libraries, Git and Google Colab. On the research side I am comfortable with qualitative and quantitative methodologies, systematic literature review, LaTeX/Overleaf and reference tools (Mendeley, Zotero, EndNote, ResearchRabbit, NotebookLM). Together with a Springer-published paper, three journal-manuscript contributions, supervision of 4 capstone projects and a year of AI/LLM quality-assurance work, this makes me a strong fit for doctoral research on trustworthy, safe AI.

🌐 Languages: English (IELTS 6.5) | German (A2)   📍 Mülheim an der Ruhr, Germany

Motivation & Passion

My passion is making AI systems that people can trust. Building 1D-CNN code-clone detectors, testing chatbot and LLM features in production platforms, and supervising privacy-preserving federated learning for healthcare showed me that powerful models need rigorous verification, robustness analysis and failure analysis. I want to pursue a PhD on LLMs and generative AI, and on agentic, safe and trustworthy AI for software engineering . My long-term goal is to publish in top-tier venues, author books, and grow into a leading scientist in the field. I am a disciplined self-learner (German A2 by self-study) and I keep moving forward on this path with persistence and enthusiasm.

MS Software Engineering

COMSATS University Islamabad · Feb 2021 – Mar 2023

Thesis: Code Clone Analysis and Detection for Software Quality Assurance Using CNN.

  • Preprocessed BigCloneBench through lexical analysis, tokenization, parsing and fragment extraction.
  • Threshold-based similarity analysis to find duplicate and near-duplicate code.
  • Developed a 1D-CNN that learns features from tokenized code; compared with conventional ML on precision, recall and detection performance.
